sources.name: Try. Capture. Share. · Pop-up brief
sources.text:
An independently authored fictional demo, not an official Meta event, commission or partnership. Dimensions and quantities are design assumptions, not measured capacity or safety validation.

Objective: Give first-time visitors in their twenties and thirties a 20-minute journey through trying on glasses, hands-free photography, open-ear listening and sharing with friends. Use the entire approximately 590 m² ground floor in Seongsu.

Program: One check-in counter; two four-seat fitting bars with mirrors; a photo walk with three photo spots; an eight-seat listening lounge; two semi-enclosed Messenger demo booths; one shared photo wall; one consultation and pickup counter.

Journey: Angled entrance → check-in → fitting bars → photo walk between columns → listening lounge → Messenger booths and photo wall in the annex → consultation and pickup. Keep the main route at least 1.5m clear. Use the south service door and storage for staff and stock.

Drawing: The north main hall is approximately 32 × 15m with a 4.2m assumed ceiling; the southeast annex is approximately 18 × 7m with a 3.6m assumed ceiling. Preserve the three 0.6m square columns. Keep the north shopfront and east windows visible. Ceiling heights are drawing assumptions; suspended loads are unreviewed. Do not furnish the toilets or storage.

Direction: Warm off-white surfaces, black lines inspired by acetate frames, and bright street-like lighting. Low walls, plants and signs create small Seongsu-inspired photo scenes.

Request: Design the entire floor with actual furniture and partitions, connecting the experiences with a one-way visitor journey.
sources.notes: Authored fictional venue and brief. Muse performed the drawing reading and design; no operations or safety simulation is included.

sources.name: AI glasses fitting bar · Authored concept
sources.text: A long off-white fitting counter with a black worktop and base, approximately 4m × 1.2m and 1.05m high. A walnut-toned tray holds demonstration glasses; three black-framed mirror panels stand behind it. Three black stools with brown cushions and a brass foot rail illustrate fitting, mirror checks and staff guidance in one furniture unit. This does not reproduce the product design.
sources.notes: Concept image drawn with repository script web/scripts/build-sample-popup.mjs. No external product photos, brand photos or logos. Width and seat counts are planning assumptions.

sources.name: Creator Connection Day · Event brief
sources.text:
An independently authored fictional demo, not an official Meta event, commission or partnership. Dimensions and quantities are design assumptions, not measured capacity or safety validation.

Objective: Connect Instagram visual creation and Threads public conversation in one visitor journey for content creators and local community organizers.

Program: One welcome desk; three vertical-video sets with backdrops, lights and phone stands; two editing feedback tables; four topic-based conversation tables; one talk stage with 24 audience chairs; one lounge; one equipment store.

Journey: Registration → capture → editing feedback → conversations → rest. Separate photo queues from stage access. Avoid directing photo lights at conversation seating. Leave accessible routes and seats for waiting visitors.

Drawing: Use only an approximately 40 × 30m area inside Hall 1B, not the full 171 × 63m hall. Leave the remaining area empty.

Direction: A bright production studio for Instagram and a calm conversation salon for Threads. This is an authored interpretation, not an official brand guide.

Request: Confirm the event area and scale, then arrange actual furniture and partitions for review. Do not automatically fill the entire hall.
sources.notes: Authored demo brief. Muse reads the drawing; no layout, operations or safety simulation is included.

sources.name: Creator display pod · Generated concept
sources.text:
A purple arched backdrop, low coral plinth and small shelf form a compact capture/display module. Color, soft edges and open sightlines inform the design. The actual layout reinterprets the reference using supported partitions, plinths and shelves; it does not claim to reproduce identical curves.

An assumed width of 1.5m is a starting point, not a photographic measurement. Height, depth and stability need separate review.
sources.notes: Fictional display concept generated from an original prompt on 2026-11-02. Not a product photograph, official brand design or 3D reconstruction. No external logos or photos were supplied. Form, material and color reference only; fabrication is unverified.
